Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 1: Commentary on the very Zohar (I 128b-129a) Rav Tzadok quotes: Machpelah/Jerusalem 'bound above and bound below, therefore doubled'; reads the doubling as Malchut receiving and giving, not as the upper and lower Heh.

Explains the same Zohar: the field, not the cave, is 'doubled'; Jerusalem above and below aligned and bound to each other. Mostly about Adam and Eve's burial, so shares only the Jerusalem-doubling step.
Sarah merited Machpelah ('zamemah sadeh vatikachehu') by a life of cleaving to her root; Machpelah is the Heh of the Name, upper and lower Heh: the same reading as Rav Tzadok's.

Asks Rav Tzadok's exact question (Sarah never knew of Machpelah; why is it credited to her?) and answers with the Zohar's two Hehs, upper and lower worlds; Sarah 'lifted' the field (11:8) and Shabbat is the model (11:9).

Same question on 'zamemah sadeh'; Machpelah = the doubled Heh, Sarah's quality of separating from this world; and it ties this to the custom of saying Eishes Chayil on Friday night with the neshamah yeseirah, Rav Tzadok's opening.
Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Gevurot Hashem 33:79-81
פירושים והערות מהרב יהושע הרטמן על גבורות השם

Quotes Pri Tzaddik (Vaera 10, Devarim 10, Pesach 47) that the ten plagues ran from below to above, 'negof ve-rafo', and at the tenth Israel left the beginning of the husk for Keter: the same idea, though from Rav Tzadok himself.
'Zamemah sadeh' = Sarah's lifelong thought to join the lower to the upper, the 'field which God has blessed' raised to the upper world; 've-natlah' = lifting. Machpelah is the place of that joining.

Machpelah per the Zohar is the joining of the two Hehs (Binah, hidden world; Malchut, revealed world); Abraham understood it came by Sarah's merit, so she is 'the one who took it' though already dead: Rav Tzadok's answer.
'Zamemah sadeh' read as Sarah's lifelong aim, brought from potential to act after death; Machpelah rises into holiness, and Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come.
Rav Bruna's joining redemption to prayer is the yichud required of the complete worshipper, so his joy lasted all day: a Kabbalistic reading of the same Gemara (Rav Tzadok: revelation of Atika).
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 2: Explains Machpelah as the lower hei receiving from the upper hei and why Avraham said 'cave' to the sons of Heth; supports Rav Tzadok's 'hei doubled', not his yirah/Hittite thesis.
The very Zohar (127b-129a) Rav Tzadok cites (notes 1, 7, 12, 48); adds that Ephron saw only darkness there since it was not his, which underlies 'captive among the sons of Heth'.
Only after Avraham completed his tikkun did the field 'rise', redeemed from the impurity of the sons of Heth; also Yitzchak as din/'pachad Yitzchak'.
Same Zohar 129a (doubled hei) and 127 (gate of Gan Eden): Machpelah joins upper and lower hei, upper and lower worlds; Sarah's wholeness ties her to it.
Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 1:8-9
A creature's name in the Holy Tongue is the vessel of its vitality, drawn down from the Ten Utterances: exactly Rav Tzadok's 'name = root of vitality' linked to the ten maamaros.
Likutei Halakhot, Choshen Mishpat, Laws of Gifting 4:11
Under Ephron the kelipos surrounded Machpelah's great holiness; Avraham drew it out by full payment and 'the field rose': the holiness held captive by the sons of Heth and released.
While the field was in Ephron's domain holiness could not rest there; once Avraham's name was on it, 'it rose'.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 3: כהדא עגלתא as every part of a life joined to its inner point, so that 'their years are whole' and each year is bound to the next; Sarah was never separated from the root of life for a moment. The same reading of the circle-calf as the equality and wholeness of all the tzaddik's years, from the Izhbitz circle's contemporary.

Explains the doubled שני חיי שרה as a second, lasting dimension of her years (the sanctified body), which is why they are dear in this world and the next: the same exegetical problem (the repetition = dearness in the World to Come), with a different answer.

Asks why the Midrash adds 'whole in her deeds' and the calf image for Sarah and not Abraham, and answers that Abraham's wholeness came from intellect while Sarah's came from the body and deeds; a parallel to Rav Tzadok's question why this is hinted in Sarah and not in Abraham.
Abraham repaired Adam's sin and Sarah repaired Eve's; the same pairing on which the maamar builds Sarah's uniqueness ('a woman among all these I have not found').

Maharal on 'Torah scholars have no rest... in the World to Come': Torah understanding has no completion, so the scholar keeps going מחיל אל חיל even there. This is Rav Tzadok's premise that life is added to scholars after death.
The tzaddik goes from level to level without end, never resting at any level of understanding, in this world or the next (Berachos 64a); the same reading of the Gemara that Rav Tzadok needs.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 4: Reads David's five 'ברכי נפשי' as the five parts of the soul, nefesh to yechidah, and ties them to BR 14's 'five names', which is Rav Tzadok's opening equation; it then turns to five corresponding impurities.
Yakar MiPaz, Insights on Haftarah, Vayishlach 2

The five levels come in stages through life (ruach at thirteen, then neshamah, chayah, yechidah), and nefesh-ruach-neshamah-chayah correspond to the letters of Havayah and yechidah to the tip of the Yud: both the mapping and the staged-life reading of this os.
Zaken = acquired wisdom, and 'ba ba-yamim' = entering the inner light of the days, the first-day light hidden for the righteous: the same pairing of zaken with the hidden light and the supernal days.

The upper worlds are called 'days'; Abraham 'zaken' acquired wisdom and 'ba ba-yamim' reached the upper worlds: the same reading as Rav Tzadok's ביומין עלאין, without his refinement of the attributes.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 5: On Shabbat 56b ('his wives turned his heart … and he did not go'): even an inclination too fine to notice counts as 'his heart was not whole'. This matches the maamar's Solomon, whose heart was turned before he noticed; the teshuvah/zaken reading is not there.
Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Gevurot Hashem 29:99-103
פירושים והערות מהרב יהושע הרטמן על גבורות השם

Brings together Abraham's self-taught Torah ('av lo limdo', his kidneys as two rabbis) and Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot BM 87a): 'ein zaken ela she-kanah chochmah', so 'until Abraham there was no old age'. This is the maamar's own Abraham = zaken through Torah from within.
Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Derush al HaTorah 19:24-27
פירושים והערות מהרב יהושע הרטמן על דרוש על התורה

Maharal on 'ein zaken ela mi she-kanah chochmah' and 'talmidei chachamim … chochmah nitosefet bahem': old age as the gaining of wisdom. The derash is the same, though Maharal grounds it in bodily powers weakening.

Abraham's wisdom deep in his kidneys ('yo'atzot oto u-melamdot oto chochmah') is a Torah of chesed that Eliezer drew out for others. The maamar pairs 'kelayot yo'atzot' with the Oral Torah as 'Torat chesed' taught to students.

'Zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah' read as wisdom rooted above, and 'ba ba-yamim' as entering the inner light of the days. This is the maamar's pairing of zaken = acquired wisdom with 'ba ba-yamim' as the supernal days.
Beit Aharon, Teachings on Torah and Holidays, R' Aharon (the Second) of Karlin, Genesis, Chayei Sara 3

Abraham's 'zaken' is the wisdom he acquired, 'ba ba-yamim' is binding all his middot to that wisdom, and only then 'Bakol' ('bat … u-Vakol shemah'). This is the maamar's order exactly: zaken = kanah chochmah, refined in all the middot, then 'blessed in all'.

Reads 'zaken ba ba-yamim' as Abraham being raised to the upper world, and 'bat … u-Vakol shemah' as the receiving lower realm (a 'midah u-mekabel') made fit for blessing. This is close to the maamar's 'Bakol' = Malchut after 'yomin ila'in'.

'Zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah' with 'bi-yeshishim chochmah': wisdom that has settled and is fixed (be-kevi'ut), with all the days whole. This matches the maamar's wisdom 'engraved on the heart permanently' and 'full of days'.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 6: The very Zohar Rav Tzadok quotes: Solomon's wisdom over the children of the East, who are the concubines' sons; the mountains of the East teach sorcery; Laban, Beor, Balaam came from there.
Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Be'er HaGolah, Well 2 4:94-102
פירושים והערות מהרב יהושע הרטמן על באר הגולה

Cites Gur Aryeh that the 'names of impurity' were not sorcery (forbidden) but demon-lore, and Menachot 85a Yochana and Mamre as Egypt's chief sorcerers (Rashi); the same two sources and the same difficulty Rav Tzadok raises.
Same puzzle in Zevachim 62b, also read as R. Tarfon's deliberate hint the nephews missed ('Yochani' = יוכני, prepare me; 'Keturah' = bound above); a different content, the same move.
Keturah is Hagar who strayed to her father's idols and then bound herself to fit deeds; the maamar's 'modest in deeds, yet Egyptian at root'.
Divrei Emet, Divrei Emet on Torah, Balak 7

The Chozeh of Lublin (from the Maggid of Rovno): 'ותרב חכמת שלמה' means Solomon took wisdom from everything; the wisdom of the children of the East and of Egypt helped his wisdom grow. Rav Tzadok's own reading of ותרב as 'grew by' what he drew out of them.

Solomon grew wise because he first learned the wisdom of the children of the East and so knew light's advantage over darkness; therefore his wisdom is 'chochmah tata'ah', a receiving wisdom. Same pairing of Solomon's lower wisdom with drawing from the East, and light out of darkness.

On the same parashah: 'ותרב חכמת שלמה מכל בני קדם' may mean that from the very wisdoms of the evil inclination true wisdom increased ('who is wise? one who learns from every man'). Same reading of the verse, applied to the yetzer rather than the nations' hidden Oral Torah.

Maharal raises Rav Tzadok's exact difficulty: Abraham cannot have given them sorcery, which the Torah punishes, so 'names of impurity' meant only demon-lore or remedies against sorcery. Rav Tzadok solves the same problem otherwise, with Paneach Raza's 'a Name in impurity'.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 7: Quotes and develops the same Zohar (Chayei Sarah 131b) the maamar expounds: Torah is all life in both worlds, frees from the Angel of Death, and 'the evil serpent that darkened the world cannot rule' over one who toils in it.

Eliezer relies on Abraham's merit to bring about the miraculous match, as in the Zohar the maamar cites ('zechuteih de-Avraham'); but it denies the test was about Rebecca's kindness, which the maamar stresses.

Commentary on the very Zohar passage ('de-oraita kol chayin... chayin de-inun chayin'): long days in the World to Come come from Arich Anpin; Rav Tzadok likewise traces this life to Atika. It also takes up the question about Moses.
Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Derush al HaTorah 18:13-14
פירושים והערות מהרב יהושע הרטמן על דרוש על התורה
Brings Bava Batra 16b-17a with Maharal (Derekh Chayyim 6): the Patriarchs' taste of the World to Come was from their own share there, with no break. This is the same derashah the maamar uses.
Quotes the same Yerushalmi 'liba ve-eina... hen yahavt li libach ve-einach' (at 7:23) and makes the heart the root; the maamar uses it on 'ha'er eineinu... ve-dabek libenu'.
Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume II, Derush I 1:5-6

Expounds the Bnei Heichala song at the third meal ('le-mechezei ziv Ze'ir Anpin', 'ra'ava de-ra'avin') as the hour of 'nachalat Yaakov'; the maamar likewise makes the third meal Jacob's time of favor.

Reads 'lech lecha' with the same Zohar 'le-atkana darga dilach' as moving from 'amidah' (acceptance of the yoke) to 'halichah', cleaving in love. This is Rav Tzadok's moving rather than standing, as Abraham's attribute of love.
The Piaseczner: one who has not grown this year has not really lived it; 'Avraham zaken ba bayamim': the Abraham of today, not of yesterday. Same reading of a life counted only by continual growth.
Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 4

The doubled 'chayei Avraham asher chai' means life drawn from supernal Chochmah through Torah ('ha-chochmah techayeh'); parallels the maamar's 'asher chai' as life from its source through Torah, though it says Chochmah where Rav Tzadok says Atika.

On Bava Batra 16b-17a: the Patriarchs tasted their own share of the World to Come in this world, with no break as the World to Come has none. This is the bakol/mikol/kol derashah the maamar applies to the three Patriarchs.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 9: Yakar MiPaz, Insights on Haftarah, Chayei Sara

The same haftarah verses (I Kings 1:5-6) read as self-satisfied pride: Adoniyahu 'סובר שהוא כבר איש תם וישר', so God sent him no humbling grief. It adds that even the crown one gives Hashem is His ('כתר כל הכתרים'). This is the same diagnosis and close to the maamar's crowning theme, although it reads 'ולא עצבו' differently.
Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 1

Explains the same Zohar: the truly great (Moshe) holds himself small, and the small hold themselves great. The higher level is nearer to unity, and the first three (ג"ר) lie above the seven days of building, which matches Rav Tzadok's 100/20/7 mapping.

Maharal on Chullin 89a: Israel's greatness is divine, so the more of it they have, the humbler they become; the nations' greatness is physical, so they grow proud. This is exactly the maamar's Israel/nations section.
Joins the same Zohar ('מאן דאיהו זעיר איהו רב') with Sotah 5a ('אין אני והוא'): because Moshe was humble the Shechinah dwelt with him, and what 'לית ליה מגרמיה כלום' receives all blessing.

Reads 'באים בימים' as 'עאלו ביומין עלאין': Avraham and Sarah could not bear children until they entered the supernal days. This is the maamar's reason why Yitzchak's birth needed parents already refined in the first three.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 10: Midrash HaNe'elam on Aravot, which holds the treasuries of good life and 'many treasuries' (ganzim). It asks how there can be one otzar and also many ganzim, the same tension Rav Tzadok resolves with otzar vs. beit genazav, though its answer (two storehouses of souls) is different.
Sha'arei Orah, Third and Fourth Gates, Seventh and Eight Sefirah 63-67
The same chain as Rav Tzadok: Moed Katan 28a children-life-sustenance hang on the Mazal, which is Keter above the Name Havayah; Channah prayed 'על ה'' and 'השלך על ה' יהבך' mean above the Name.

Raises the same contradiction (the Shabbat gift in His treasure-house vs. 'nothing but an otzar of fear of Heaven') and resolves it as Rav Tzadok does: the Shabbat treasury is included in the otzar of fear of Heaven, through 'ירא שבת'.
Children, life and sustenance depend on Mazal, and holy Shabbat is that Mazal; the three Shabbat meals draw down children, life and sustenance, as in the maamar's close.
The 'otzar of fear of Heaven' is a receiving vessel (kli kibbul) for supernal Chochmah, close to Rav Tzadok's point that an otzar is the vessel that holds His treasures.
Likutei Halakhot, Orach Chaim, Laws for Morning Blessings 5:26:1

'You are One' is said at Shabbat Minchah because the Holy One, the Torah and Israel are then one, joined to 'מנוחת שלום ושלוה השקט ובטח'. This parallels Rav Tzadok's reading of 'Atah Echad' as the union of Hashem and Israel, though it stresses love among Israel.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 11: Asks Rav Tzadok's exact question (why wake them with this derasha, and why R. Akiva); answers (§76) that R. Akiva's derasha aims to bind himself to his dozing generation and raise them, which needs their will: close in purpose, different mechanism.
Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1-4

Explains the same waking: the dozing is weariness from hester panim (exile); Esther = hiddenness, yet she reigns by Sarah's merit, so they should trust God in the dark. Same question, different answer (and fn 36 already notes its 'kulan shavin le-tovah' as a contrast).

Nearly Rav Tzadok's reading: R. Akiva expounded lofty things and people dozed because they thought they could not live up to them; he woke them with Sarah, whose years even at 100 like 20 were all sanctified, though she was exempt from time-bound mitzvot.
Reads the Tanna Devei Eliyahu obligation exactly as Rav Tzadok's ending does: it forbids the false humility of 'who am I to seek great things', which the Satan plants to idle a person from Torah.
In the name of the Pshischa: no fool compares himself to the Patriarchs; 'yagi'u' means one's deeds touch and cleave to the Patriarchs' deeds; parallels Rav Tzadok's 'at least in some particular'.

'The deeds of my fathers that they planted in me': the Patriarchs prepared knowledge and longing for all Israel, to be awakened in their offspring; Rav Tzadok's 'they planted in the heart of their offspring'.

States the same equation Rav Tzadok draws from Esther's verse: ruach hakodesh is the aspect of Malchut ('va-tilbash Esther malchut... she was clothed in ruach hakodesh'), applied to Torah and prayer spoken in attachment to Malchut.
Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 8: Asks what ראש לנסיון in BR 59:6 means and why Joshua is 'head' of Ephraim's kingship; answers that Abraham, Joshua and David are 'samples' of what God will raise later — Joshua and David prefigure the two Mashiachs of Ephraim and Judah. Same Midrash, same question, and the same Mashiach ben Yosef/ben David resolution as Rav Tzadok's close.

No tzaddik truly dies; the past days of David and Abraham (והמלך דוד זקן בא בימים / ואברהם זקן בא בימים) remain 'alive and enduring'. Links the two verses of the haftarah and parashah to the living permanence Rav Tzadok reads in דוד מלך ישראל חי וקיים.
Because David broke his sleep for God, even his sleep has life: 'דוד מלך ישראל חי וקיים ומותא לא שריא עליו'. Parallels Rav Tzadok's claim that David never died but only sleeps for a time.

Maharal on the same Midrash (זקן שקנה שני עולמים; בפילון מפולש): the 'open gateway' is the straight, unswerving path to the World to Come, aligned with the Yud. Gives the sense of the phrase Rav Tzadok cites for Abraham's refinement to the supernal days.
